question: What happened to Project Xanadu last Tuesday, and why did it happen?

claims.text: Assuming "last Tuesday" is August 25, 2026, the supplied evidence says there was no good web evidence of a new public Project Xanadu event on that date.
acceptable_patterns: Assuming[\s\S]*August 25, 2026[\s\S]*no good web evidence of a new public Project Xanadu event on that date
no good web evidence of a new public Project Xanadu event on that date

evidence_passages.text: Assuming “last Tuesday” means August 25, 2026 ... I found no good web evidence of a new public Project Xanadu event on that date.

claims.text: The clearly dated August 25, 2026 Xanadu news in the supplied evidence was about Xanadu Quantum Technologies and Mitsubishi Chemical, not about Project Xanadu.
acceptable_patterns: clearly dated[\s\S]*August 25, 2026[\s\S]*about Xanadu Quantum Technologies and Mitsubishi Chemical[\s\S]*not about Project Xanadu
Canada-Japan Funding Fuels Xanadu and Mitsubishi Chemical Partnership on Quantum Semiconductor Research

evidence_passages.text: The clearly dated August 25, 2026 “Xanadu” news I did find was about Xanadu Quantum Technologies and Mitsubishi Chemical expanding a quantum-semiconductor collaboration, not about Project Xanadu.

rejected_claims.text: Project Xanadu definitely had no activity at all last Tuesday.
rejected_claims.reason: Unsupported and too absolute. The supplied evidence says only that no good web evidence was found and explicitly notes this does not prove nothing happened privately or off-web.

rejected_claims.text: Project Xanadu shut down last Tuesday.
rejected_claims.reason: Unsupported. No supplied evidence reports a shutdown.

rejected_claims.text: Ted Nelson died last Tuesday, causing a Project Xanadu event.
rejected_claims.reason: Unsupported and contradictory to the supplied evidence; no supplied passage documents such an event.

rejected_claims.text: The August 25, 2026 Xanadu news was about Project Xanadu's own announcement.
rejected_claims.reason: Contradicted by the supplied evidence, which says the clearly dated August 25, 2026 Xanadu news was about Xanadu Quantum Technologies and Mitsubishi Chemical, not Project Xanadu.

rejected_claims.text: The supplied evidence describes the Project Xanadu web pages it found as old or archival rather than showing a dated August 2026 Project Xanadu announcement.
rejected_claims.reason: Depends on page-level details (the 'crudcheck 01.05.23' marker, 'WE FIGHT ON' message, 'Last-modified: 2002/04/12' on aus.xanadu.com/xanadu/faq.html, and the 'Future of Text Conference, August 25, 2016' demo page) for which the supplied evidence contains no retrieved content. The Codex run's opened_urls is empty and every tool_result states the search payload was not exposed; its evidence_passages are just its own final_answer duplicated under five URLs, so they do not attest to what those pages say. The Claude run corroborates only xanadu.com/xuhome.html and never touches aus.xanadu.com/xanadu/faq.html or xanadu.com/xuDemoPage.html. The third acceptable_pattern ('web presence[\s\S]*historical rather than actively updated') also grades an interpretive characterization rather than a checkable fact.

rejected_claims.text: The most defensible conclusion in the supplied evidence is that nothing well-documented and publicly notable appears to have happened to Project Xanadu itself last Tuesday, and there is no solid public event evidence to explain why.
rejected_claims.reason: Explicitly the run's inference layer ('most defensible conclusion', 'likeliest explanation') rather than anything the cited sources state; the three listed sources are archival Project Xanadu pages that cannot support a conclusion about last Tuesday, and two of them (aus.xanadu.com/xanadu/faq.html, xanadu.com/xuDemoPage.html) have no verified content anywhere in the evidence. It also restates the supported negative finding already carried by claim_no_public_event_evidence, and its grading is brittle: both acceptable_patterns require long verbatim teacher wording, and required_concepts such as 'most_defensible_conclusion' and 'why' are too vague to grade deterministically.
